name: Kiro CLI
notes: Reference adapter. Every capability exercised in a multi-week production run.

resume.note: Injects into the same store the IDE uses; the IDE panel may not render an externally started turn even though it runs correctly.

transcript.workspace_hash: opaque per-workspace directory; resolve via list_sessions cwd match

busy.note: status can remain in_progress across an idle gap; the mtime check is the reliable half.

mcp.register_note: run only when the CLI is installed and the file does not exist yet; otherwise the entry is merged

steering_inclusion.unhonoured: Kiro CLI 2.x, which this adapter runs, supports no inclusion mode and loads every steering file in every session; fileMatch, manual and auto hold in the IDE, and the first two in the 3.0 early release
steering_inclusion.note: Modes: always, the default; fileMatch with fileMatchPattern, one pattern or a list; manual, included by #name in chat; auto, with name and description. Workspace steering is .kiro/steering and global steering ~/.kiro/steering; AGENTS.md is always loaded; a custom agent loads steering only through its resources. The steering page says Kiro CLI supports no inclusion mode and loads every steering file, while its capability table marks always, fileMatch and manual for the CLI: the 3.0 early release (kiro-cli --v3, beside 2.x) adds that front matter, and leaves auto to the engine. send and resume run 2.x, the newest CLI in the changelog being 2.21.4 of 2026-09-11. Read from kiro.dev/docs/steering, kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3 and kiro.dev/changelog/cli on 2026-09-17.

commands.hooks: hooks are never imported: each runs a command when its trigger fires
commands.mcpServers: an MCP server is a command the CLI starts: never imported

grants.allowedTools: the tools it uses without asking
grants.toolsSettings: the paths and commands its tools may use without asking
grants.permissions: the rules that allow or deny what its tools may do

context.empty: a custom agent loads no steering and no skills unless its resources name them

agent_format.note: Workspace agents are .kiro/agents/<name>.json and global ones ~/.kiro/agents, the workspace's winning by name; name defaults to the file name and prompt is inline or a file:// URI. Fields: name, description, prompt, model, tools, toolAliases, allowedTools, toolsSettings, resources (file://, skill://, knowledgeBase), mcpServers, useLegacyMcpJson or includeMcpJson, hooks (agentSpawn, userPromptSubmit, preToolUse, postToolUse, stop), keyboardShortcut, welcomeMessage. The IDE ignores an agent's hooks. The 3.0 early release (kiro-cli --v3) reads a universal format that 2.x reads too (/upgrade-agent writes it), replaces toolsSettings with permissions, reads Markdown agents with YAML front matter as the IDE does, and moves hooks to .kiro/hooks. Read from kiro.dev/docs/custom-agents/configuration-reference and kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3 on 2026-09-17.

hook_files..kiro.hook: an IDE hook in the 0.x format (when, then), which Kiro CLI does not read

directives.warning: File triggers fire only for changes made by the agent itself. A message dropped by an external process will NOT fire PostFileCreate — use SessionStart plus steering instead.

balance.note: Plan balance is not written to disk. Never estimated; use keyflip for real quota windows.

failure.note: Structural verdict on every tool result. Never text-match for 'error' or 'failed' — the agent's own search patterns and passing test names contain both.

api.auth: Bearer <access_token> from the CLI's own store
api.token_store: ~/Library/Application Support/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3, auth_kv where key='kirocli:odic:token', field access_token
api.response: usageBreakdownList[resourceType=CREDIT].currentUsageWithPrecision and .usageLimitWithPrecision; plus subscriptionInfo, overageConfiguration, nextDateReset, daysUntilReset

billing.api_key_note: A ksk_ API key is NOT a bearer token for this endpoint — it is rejected with AccessDeniedException on codewhisperer and 'Invalid token' on management.kiro.dev. It authenticates the CLI via KIRO_API_KEY. The CLI's cached OIDC access token is what works here.

fallback.note: Each usage_summary closes one turn and carries that turn's whole cost, so the records add up. Measured on one machine's store, July to September 2026: 455 records and never two for one turn, no request id shared by two consecutive records, and the older records that carry no request ids never two for one turn either. The peak-per-turn reading declared here before took a drop between two records for a new turn and read 79% of the sum; each session's last record alone reads under 1% of it.
fallback.accuracy: a floor: sessions on other machines are invisible. The 69% of the account figure recorded here was measured under the peak-per-turn reading; the sum has not been measured against the account.

models._note: Kiro picks its own model; --model passes one through when set
